summary.en: Read tokens and lines, format decimal values and choose Scanner or BufferedReader.
summary.bn: টোকেন আর পুরো লাইন পড়ুন, দশমিক সাজান এবং দরকারমতো ইনপুট টুল বেছে নিন।

notes: Scanner dates from Java 5; String.isBlank used with buffered input needs Java 11 or later.

sections.title: Agree on what enters and what leaves
Tokens and lines are different units
Control presentation without changing the value
Do not confuse a line with a value
Match the parser to the input agreement

examples.title: Read two marks
examples.explanationHtml: The two tokens become int values. The prompt stays beside the total because it uses print.

examples.title: A number followed by a full line
examples.explanationHtml: The extra nextLine consumes the remaining newline after the roll. The following call reads the whole name.

examples.title: A fixed decimal format
examples.explanationHtml: %.2f prints two digits after the decimal point. Locale.ROOT fixes the decimal separator.

examples.title: Sum integers until input ends
examples.explanationHtml: The loop reads all three integer tokens and stops at the end, giving 15.

examples.title: Buffered line input
examples.explanationHtml: readLine returns text without its line ending. Each nonblank line is parsed as one integer, giving 12.

practice.title: Read a full course title
practice.statementHtml: Input: one line, possibly empty. Print Course: followed by the entire line.

practice.title: Total until EOF
practice.statementHtml: Input: zero or more integers from 0 to 100, with total at most 100000. Print their sum.
hints: Check before consuming the next token.

practice.title: Print a decimal bill
practice.statementHtml: Input: one nonnegative decimal amount at most 100000 using a dot. Print BDT and exactly two fractional digits.
hints: Set the locale for both reading and writing.

practice.title: Roll and full name
practice.statementHtml: Input: an integer roll on one line and a nonempty full name on the next. Print the roll, one space and the full name.
hints: Consume the rest of the number line before reading the name.

practice.title: Count nonblank lines
practice.statementHtml: Input: zero or more lines. With BufferedReader, count lines whose trimmed content is nonempty. Print the count.
hints: Do not confuse an empty line with null.

quiz.prompt: Which fractional digits does printf keep for this mark average?
quiz.explanation: Decimal division gives 3.5 and %.2f pads it to 3.50.

quiz.prompt: Does String.format print by itself or return a formatted label?
quiz.explanation: %03d pads the integer to width three with leading zeros, giving Roll 007.

quiz.prompt: How does println separate two calls compared with print?
quiz.explanation: print leaves A on the current line; println adds B before ending it, then C starts a new line.

quiz.prompt: After nextInt reads 17 before a newline, what does nextLine usually return?
options: The remaining empty part of that line
quiz.explanation: nextInt leaves the line separator unread. nextLine consumes the remainder of the current line.

quiz.prompt: Which Scanner method reads a whitespace-separated word?
quiz.explanation: next reads a token, while nextLine reads a line remainder.

quiz.prompt: What does hasNextInt return at the end of an integer stream?
quiz.explanation: There is no next integer token, so the boolean check is false.
An empty String means an empty line exists. null means no more line can be read.

quiz.prompt: Why use Locale.ROOT when decimal text must contain a dot?
options: It converts every number to int
Formatting can otherwise depend on the default locale
quiz.explanation: Locale chooses conventions such as decimal separators; it does not change numeric precision.
parseInt converts text to int and rejects invalid integer text.

quiz.prompt: Why might BufferedReader suit a large line-based input?
options: It buffers character reading with little token-parsing overhead
quiz.explanation: You gain control over parsing and can avoid Scanner token-processing costs.

quiz.prompt: Why can hasNextInt be false before actual EOF?
options: The Scanner always reads only one token
The next token may not be a valid integer
quiz.explanation: hasNextInt tests whether the next token can be parsed as int, not only whether any input remains.

quiz.prompt: Why avoid two independent buffered readers over System.in?
options: They may buffer parts of the same stream separately
quiz.explanation: Readers can consume ahead, making input ownership confusing. Coordinate one reader per stream.

keyPoints.en: Scanner reads tokens according to its parsing rules.
keyPoints.bn: Scanner নিজের পার্সিং নিয়ম মেনে টোকেন পড়ে।

keyPoints.en: nextLine reads the rest of the current line.
keyPoints.bn: nextLine বর্তমান লাইনের বাকি অংশ পড়ে।

keyPoints.en: hasNextInt can control an integer-reading loop.
keyPoints.bn: hasNextInt দিয়ে পূর্ণসংখ্যা পড়ার লুপ নিয়ন্ত্রণ করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: A fixed locale keeps decimal formatting predictable.
keyPoints.bn: নির্দিষ্ট লোকেল দিলে দশমিক লেখার ধরন ঠিক থাকে।

keyPoints.en: BufferedReader returns null when no more lines remain.
keyPoints.bn: আর লাইন না থাকলে BufferedReader থেকে null আসে।

keyPoints.en: String.format returns text while printf writes it.
keyPoints.bn: String.format লেখা ফেরত দেয়, আর printf সরাসরি লেখে।

examQuestions.question: Explain the nextInt followed by nextLine trap and its repair.
examQuestions.answerHtml: nextInt consumes the numeric token but leaves the line ending. The next nextLine reads the remaining part, often empty. Consume that remainder before reading the intended following line.

examQuestions.question: Give an EOF loop plan for one integer per line using BufferedReader.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Read a line until readLine returns null. Skip blank lines if the input policy allows them. Trim and parse each remaining line, add the value to a bounded total, then print after the loop.

examQuestions.question: Compare printf and String.format with the same format pattern.
examQuestions.answerHtml: printf writes formatted text to the output stream. String.format returns formatted text that can be saved or printed later. Both accept an explicit locale.
